Using logistic regression with Age as the only predictor (fit on all 80 patients, y = 1 if Efficacy=='PR' else 0, standard intercept), the predicted probability of achieving efficacy PR at age 65 is 0.3952 (≈ 39.52%).

Model details (statsmodels Logit, MLE):
- n = 80 patients, 41 PR events
- Intercept (beta0) = 4.4466
- Slope (beta1, Age) = -0.07495
- Log-likelihood = -50.0710
- Linear predictor at Age=65 = 4.4466 + (-0.07495)(65) = -0.42544
- Inverse-logit → P(PR | Age=65) = 0.395216 ≈ 0.3952

The negative slope reflects that older patients were less likely to be in the PR (treatment-response) group.
